item.title: 🔴 How to contain shadow AI, as it takes on multiple forms and spreads throughout your environment
item.description:
Why this matters: Advanced threat activity — review privileged access, persistence detection, and lateral-movement controls.

Shadow AI used to be confined to a few simple scenarios, such as AI chatbots and AI browser extensions. Today, it spans a broad spectrum of complex vectors, making it harder to detect and control. In the latest installment of our Cybersecurity Awareness Month blog series, learn how employee security training, AI usage governance, and exposure management can help you tackle shadow AI successfully.

Key takeaways

  1. Integrating shadow AI into security awareness training helps employees recognize its risks and learn how to safely adopt AI tools. Security teams should foster open communication with employees and try to understand why they use unsanctioned AI products.
  2. Shadow AI now spans local models, AI coding assistants, autonomous agents, and many other asset types across your environment, making it a pervasive and complex problem.
  3. You can reduce shadow AI incidence by enacting an AI acceptable use policy that provides clear guidelines and a list of approved AI tools, and by addressing shadow AI as part of your unified exposure management program.

item.title: 🟠 Oracle October 2026 Critical Patch Update Addresses 1209 CVEs
item.description:
Why this matters: Supply-chain risk — review third-party access and affected vendor dependencies.

Oracle addresses 1209 CVEs in its final quarterly update of 2026 with 1295 patches, including 112 critical updates.

Key Takeaways

  1. The October 2026 Critical Patch Update (CPU) contains fixes for 1209 unique CVEs in 1295 security updates
  2. 112 issues (8.6% of all patches) were assigned a critical severity rating
  3. Oracle Fusion Middleware received the highest number of patches at 206, accounting for 15.9% of all patches

Background

On October 20, Oracle released its Critical Patch Update (CPU) for October 2026, the final quarterly update of the year. This CPU contains fixes for 1209 unique CVEs in 1295 security updates across 33 Oracle product families. Out of the 1295 security updates published this quarter, 8.6% of patches were assigned a critical severity. Medium severity patches accounted for the bulk of security patches at 47.3%, followed by high severity patches at 36.7%.

This quarter's update includes 112 critical patches across 95 CVEs.


Source: Tenable Blog  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 1d

item.title: 🔴 Your Next Insider Threat Won’t be Human: Securing AI Agents From the Outside in
item.description:
Why this matters: Elevated ransomware risk — validate backups, endpoint protection, and recovery readiness.

Why the controls on an AI agent have to live outside of it, and what a security operations team can do to implement and maintain those controls.

The new privileged user in your environment

Security teams spent two decades learning how to work with the people they trust most. Domain admins, DBAs, finance approvers and contractors with VPN access all get a mature playbook: verified identity, scoped access, logged activity and a fast way to revoke it all.

Today, we’re navigating the same kind of access with regard to AI agents. They read our mailboxes, query our data lakes, open tickets, push code and increasingly, act on production systems. Unlike a new hire, an agent can’t be interviewed, background-checked or made to sign an acceptable-use policy.

item.title: 🔴 Rapid7 Analysis: NetScaler intrusions chaining CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88779
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and watch for suspicious sign-ins.

Overview

In early October 2026, Rapid7 analysts investigated a compromise of a Citrix NetScaler ADC appliance. The appliance was running an affected 14.1 build and was exposed to active exploitation targeting NetScaler authentication and SAML deployments.

The intrusion achieved root code execution, deployed multiple persistence mechanisms, installed PHP web shells, created outbound command-and-control and internal tunnelling capabilities, performed targeted reconnaissance of DNS, LDAP/Active Directory, management services and VMware vCenter infrastructure, and exfiltrated NetScaler configuration and key material.

The activity overlaps with public reporting on the WHIPSHOT/SLAPSHOT NetScaler campaign. However, this case provides additional detail on the operational lifecycle, including repeated post-reboot execution through the crash-handling workflow, HA-aware persistence, a dedicated Go reconnaissance tool, a separate FreeBSD proxy agent, and a staged collection pipeline.

item.title: 🟠 Unmasking the robots: Why it’s critical to discover AI agent identities and how Tenable helps you secure them
item.description:
Why this matters: Potential data exposure — review monitoring and incident-response readiness.

Discover how to secure AI agents in your cloud environment with Tenable One Cloud Exposure. We explore Microsoft Entra Agent ID and provide essential best practices for robust agentic AI identity security.

Key takeaways

  1. Understand your current maturity level and then build an appropriate action plan to secure your agent identities.
  2. Use your cloud providers’ native tools or Tenable One Cloud Exposure to locate and catalog every AI agent operating in your environment.
  3. Do not assign human identities or over-privileged service accounts to the AI agents your vendors deploy in your environment. Instead, require that vendors adopt official models like Microsoft Entra Agent ID for their AI agents’ identities.

As AI agents move from experimental toys to tools that make autonomous decisions, interact with databases, and call external APIs, organizations need to be clear on who — or what — is executing these actions in their cloud environments.

Why non-human identities (NHIs) aren’t secure enough for AI agents

Security teams categorize identities into two buckets: human identities and non-human identities (NHIs), such as service accounts, secrets, and automated scripts.

item.title: 🟠 Rapid7 Analysis: GitLab CI/CD Regex Integer Overflow (CVE-2026-97229)
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and watch for suspicious sign-ins.

Overview

On October 12, 2026, GitLab released 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8 to fix CVE-2026-97229, an integer overflow in its CI/CD regular-expression handling. The issue was reported through HackerOne by joaxcar. GitLab assigned it a CVSS score of 10.0 and described possible code execution by an unauthenticated user.
